name: Queue architecture
description: Asynchronous work split three ways: a consumer that owns delivery semantics, a job handler that owns the work, and a queue manager that owns the infrastructure and its policy.
appliesWhen: Work must happen outside a request, may be retried, and must survive the process that scheduled it.

broker.description: Which broker backs the queue. Changes the queue-manager template only; consumer and handler are unaffected by design.

handlerStyle.description: How job handlers are structured. Functional handlers are easier to test; class handlers suit handlers with several injected collaborators.

scheduling.description: Whether the architecture also schedules work. Recurring scheduling adds a leader-election concern that none of these three layers own.

incompatible.reason: A consumer that configures its own queue cannot be tested without a broker and duplicates retry policy. Inject the connection instead.
A handler that reaches back into the consumer can acknowledge its own message, which breaks the single point of delivery accounting.
